analysis: Documentation-only PR: docs/developer/desktop-app.md (lines 334-337 at head) and docs/developer/test.md (date bump, CI routing text near base 1432 and 2057-2061). No executable code, protocol, attestation, key-handling, cache or authorization behavior changes, so none of the threat-model entries (T-041, TB-011 and so on) are affected by the diff itself. The desktop-app.md change says manual dispatch of desktop.yml runs desktop-package and produces an unsigned review artifact, routed to a Darkbloom Sandbox Mac when granted and otherwise to blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27. It still states that this does not publish a release or establish attestation qualification, so it makes no overclaim. The test.md changes say all Mac jobs, now including the 3 GPU shards, are routed, and that only release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners. This implies Cluster GPU Tests move to the routed runner path (TB-013 add-on/sandbox runner context). The workflow files, scripts and the runner-routing plane are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify that routing keeps release-signing secrets and write permissions away from sandbox runners. The docs say routed jobs keep read-only permissions and release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners, which is a reasonable control, but its implementation is unverified. Integration should confirm in .github/workflows and the ci-runner-routing code that unsigned review artifact jobs and GPU shards get no signing credentials. This is a note about unverified external contracts, not a finding. The excerpt for test.md was truncated at the end, but the patch shown is complete for the changed ranges listed.
